sanskrit: sūta uvāca tato rajanyāṃ vyuṣṭāyāṃ prabhāta udite ravau kadrūś ca vinatā caiva bhaginyau te tapodhana
english: Suta said: Then, when the night had passed and dawn had broken with the sun rising, Kadrū and Vinatā, those two sisters, O sage of great austerities,

sanskrit: amarṣite susaṃrabdhe dāsye kṛtapaṇe tadā jagmatus turagaṃ draṣṭum ucchaiḥśravasam antikāt
english: both furious and deeply agitated, having made their wager with slavery as the stake, went together to see the horse Uccaiḥśravas up close.

sanskrit: dadṛśāte tadā tatra samudraṃ nidhim ambhasām timiṃgilajhaṣākīrṇaṃ makarair āvṛtaṃ tathā
english: There they beheld the ocean, that treasury of waters, teeming with timiṅgila fish and other great fish, and thronged with makaras.

sanskrit: sattvaiś ca bahusāhasrair nānārūpaiḥ samāvṛtam ugrair nityam anādhṛṣyaṃ kūrmagrāhasamākulam
english: It was filled with thousands upon thousands of creatures of many forms, fierce and ever unapproachable, swarming with tortoises and crocodiles.

sanskrit: ākaraṃ sarvaratnānām ālayaṃ varuṇasya ca nāgānām ālayaṃ ramyam uttamaṃ saritāṃ patim
english: It was the mine of all jewels, the abode of Varuṇa, the beautiful and supreme dwelling place of the nāgas, the lord of rivers.

sanskrit: pātālajvalanāvāsam asurāṇāṃ ca bandhanam bhayaṃkaraṃ ca sattvānāṃ payasāṃ nidhim arṇavam
english: It was the home of the fires of Pātāla, the prison of the asuras, terrifying to all beings — that ocean, the boundless reservoir of waters.

sanskrit: śubhaṃ divyam amartyānām amṛtasyākaraṃ param aprameyam acintyaṃ ca supuṇyajalam adbhutam
english: Auspicious and divine, the supreme source of nectar for the immortals, immeasurable and inconceivable, its waters were most holy and wondrous.

sanskrit: ghoraṃ jalacarārāvaraudraṃ bhairavanisvanam gambhīrāvartakalilaṃ sarvabhūtabhayaṃkaram
english: Terrible, with the fierce roar of its aquatic creatures, resounding with dreadful noise, its depths filled with swirling eddies, it struck terror into all beings.

sanskrit: velādolānilacalaṃ kṣobhodvegasamutthitam vīcīhastaiḥ pracalitair nṛtyantam iva sarvaśaḥ
english: Stirred by the wind that swings along the shore, agitated by turbulence and surging waves, with its billowing wave-hands it seemed to dance on every side.

sanskrit: candravṛddhikṣayavaśād udvṛttormidurāsadam pāñcajanyasya jananaṃ ratnākaram anuttamam
english: Its towering waves surging with the waxing and waning of the moon made it unapproachable; it was the birthplace of Pāñcajanya, the incomparable mine of gems.

sanskrit: gāṃ vindatā bhagavatā govindenāmitaujasā varāharūpiṇā cāntarvikṣobhitajalāvilam
english: Its waters had been churned and muddied within when the blessed Govinda of boundless might, assuming the form of a great boar, had recovered the earth.

sanskrit: brahmarṣiṇā ca tapatā varṣāṇāṃ śatam atriṇā anāsāditagādhaṃ ca pātālatalam avyayam
english: And the brahmarṣi Atri, performing austerities for a hundred years within it, had not touched its unfathomable bottom — imperishable Pātāla lay below.

sanskrit: adhyātmayoganidrāṃ ca padmanābhasya sevataḥ yugādikālaśayanaṃ viṣṇor amitatejasaḥ
english: There too was the repose of Padmanābha, Viṣṇu of boundless radiance, who at the dawn of each cosmic age sleeps the yogic slumber of deep spiritual absorption.

sanskrit: vaḍavāmukhadīptāgnes toyahavyapradaṃ śubham agādhapāraṃ vistīrṇam aprameyaṃ saritpatim
english: The water was the auspicious oblation-offering to the submarine fire blazing at the Vaḍavāmukha; the lord of rivers was fathomless in depth, vast in expanse, and beyond measure.

sanskrit: mahānadībhir bahvībhiḥ spardhayeva sahasraśaḥ abhisāryamāṇam aniśaṃ dadṛśāte mahārṇavam
english: They beheld that great ocean, approached unceasingly by thousands upon thousands of mighty rivers as if each were vying with the others.

sanskrit: gambhīraṃ timimakarograsaṃkulaṃ taṃ; garjantaṃ jalacararāvaraudranādaiḥ vistīrṇaṃ dadṛśatur ambaraprakāśaṃ; te 'gādhaṃ nidhim urum ambhasām anantam
english: They saw that ocean, deep, filled with fierce timi fish and makaras, roaring with the terrible cries of its water creatures, vast and bright as the sky, fathomless — the great, boundless treasury of waters.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ jhaṣamakarormisaṃkulaṃ taṃ; gambhīraṃ vikasitam ambaraprakāśam pātālajvalanaśikhāvidīpitaṃ taṃ; paśyantyau drutam abhipetatus tadānīm
english: Thus beholding that ocean crowded with fish, makaras, and waves, deep and expansive and luminous as the sky, lit by the tongues of the submarine Pātāla-fire, the two of them at that moment hurried swiftly forward.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca taṃ samudram atikramya kadrūr vinatayā saha nyapatat turagābhyāśe nacirād iva śīghragā
english: Suta said: Having crossed over that ocean, Kadrū, swift as thought, descended with Vinatā near the horse in no time at all.

sanskrit: niśāmya ca bahūn vālān kṛṣṇān pucchaṃ samāśritān vinatāṃ viṣaṇṇavadanāṃ kadrūr dāsye nyayojayat
english: And having observed many black hairs attached to its tail, Kadrū pressed Vinatā, whose face had fallen, into servitude.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā vinatā tasmin paṇitena parājitā abhavad duḥkhasaṃtaptā dāsībhāvaṃ samāsthitā
english: Then Vinatā, defeated by that wager, overcome with sorrow, assumed the condition of a slave.

sanskrit: etasminn antare caiva garuḍaḥ kāla āgate vinā mātrā mahātejā vidāryāṇḍam ajāyata
english: In the meantime, when the proper time arrived, the mighty Garuḍa, of great radiance, burst open his shell and was born, without his mother.

sanskrit: agnirāśir ivodbhāsan samiddho 'tibhayaṃkaraḥ pravṛddhaḥ sahasā pakṣī mahākāyo nabhogataḥ
english: Blazing like a heap of fire, fully kindled and utterly terrifying, that great-bodied bird grew in an instant and soared into the sky.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ prajāḥ sarvā vibhāvasum praṇipatyābruvaṃś cainam āsīnaṃ viśvarūpiṇam
english: Seeing him, all creatures sought refuge in Agni, bowing down and addressing him as he sat there in his universal form.

sanskrit: agne mā tvaṃ pravardhiṣṭhāḥ kaccin no na didhakṣasi asau hi rāśiḥ sumahān samiddhas tava sarpati
english: "O Agni, do not grow any further! Surely you do not wish to burn us? That great blazing mass of yours is spreading on and on!"

sanskrit: agnir uvāca naitad evaṃ yathā yūyaṃ manyadhvam asurārdanāḥ garuḍo balavān eṣa mama tulyaḥ svatejasā
english: Agni said: "It is not as you think, O slayers of asuras. This is Garuḍa, the mighty one — equal to me in his own radiance."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktās tato gatvā garuḍaṃ vāgbhir astuvan adūrād abhyupetyainaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tadā
english: Suta said: Thus addressed, the gods then went to Garuḍa and, together with the hosts of sages, approached him closely and praised him with words.

sanskrit: tvam ṛṣis tvaṃ mahābhāgas tvaṃ devaḥ patageśvaraḥ tvaṃ prabhus tapanaprakhyas tvaṃ nas trāṇam anuttamam
english: "You are a ṛṣi, you are supremely blessed, you are a god, lord of birds. You are the sovereign, blazing like the sun. You are our incomparable refuge."

sanskrit: balormimān sādhur adīnasattvaḥ; samṛddhimān duṣprasahas tvam eva tapaḥ śrutaṃ sarvam ahīnakīrte; anāgataṃ copagataṃ ca sarvam
english: "You are a wave of strength, noble, undaunted in spirit, full of prosperity, irresistible. You are austerity, you are all learning, O one of undimmed glory — all that is to come and all that has come to pass."

sanskrit: tvam uttamaḥ sarvam idaṃ carācaraṃ; gabhastibhir bhānur ivāvabhāsase samākṣipan bhānumataḥ prabhāṃ muhus; tvam antakaḥ sarvam idaṃ dhruvādhruvam
english: "You are the highest; this entire creation, moving and unmoving, shines through you as the sun illumines with its rays — eclipsing even the sun's own brilliance again and again. You are the Ender of all this, both the fixed and the unfixed."

sanskrit: divākaraḥ parikupito yathā dahet; prajās tathā dahasi hutāśanaprabha bhayaṃkaraḥ pralaya ivāgnis utthito; vināśayan yugaparivartanāntakṛt
english: "As the sun when enraged would burn all creatures, so you burn them, O one blazing like fire. You are terrifying, like the fire of dissolution arisen, destroying all, bringing about the end at the turning of the cosmic age."

sanskrit: khageśvaraṃ śaraṇam upasthitā vayaṃ; mahaujasaṃ vitimiram abhragocaram mahābalaṃ garuḍam upetya khecaraṃ; parāvaraṃ varadam ajayyavikramam
english: "We have come seeking refuge in you, lord of birds, of great might, beyond darkness, who range the clouds — we approach Garuḍa, the sky-farer, the great-armed, the boon-granter, of unconquerable valor."

sanskrit: evaṃ stutaḥ suparṇas tu devaiḥ sarṣigaṇais tadā tejasaḥ pratisaṃhāram ātmanaḥ sa cakāra ha
english: Thus praised by the gods together with the hosts of sages, Suparṇa then withdrew into himself his own blazing radiance.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tataḥ kāmagamaḥ pakṣī mahāvīryo mahābalaḥ mātur antikam āgacchat paraṃ tīraṃ mahodadheḥ
english: Suta said: Then that bird who travels at will, of great heroism and immense strength, came to his mother's side at the far shore of the great ocean.

sanskrit: yatra sā vinatā tasmin paṇitena parājitā atīva duḥkhasaṃtaptā dāsībhāvam upāgatā
english: There Vinatā, defeated in that wager, afflicted with the deepest sorrow, had assumed the state of a slave.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cid vinatāṃ pravaṇāṃ putrasaṃnidhau kāla āhūya vacanaṃ kadrūr idam abhāṣata
english: Then one day, summoning Vinatā who was bowed down in her son's presence, Kadrū addressed her with these words at an opportune moment:

sanskrit: nāgānām ālayaṃ bhadre suramyaṃ ramaṇīyakam samudrakukṣāv ekānte tatra māṃ vinate vaha
english: "O fortunate Vinatā, carry me to the delightful abode of the nāgas, beautiful and lovely, situated in a secluded part of the ocean's bosom."

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇamātā tām avahat sarpamātaram pannagān garuḍaś cāpi mātur vacanacoditaḥ
english: Then the mother of Suparṇa carried the mother of serpents, and Garuḍa too, prompted by his mother's word, carried the serpents.

sanskrit: sa sūryasyābhito yāti vainateyo vihaṃgamaḥ sūryaraśmiparītāś ca mūrcchitāḥ pannagābhavan tadavasthān sutān dṛṣṭvā kadrūḥ śakram athāstuvat
english: As Vainateya, that bird, flew close around the sun, the serpents were enveloped by the sun's rays and fell unconscious. Seeing her sons in that condition, Kadrū then praised Śakra.

sanskrit: namas te devadeveśa namas te balasūdana namucighna namas te 'stu sahasrākṣa śacīpate
english: "Salutation to you, O lord of the lords of gods! Salutation to you, O slayer of Bala! Salutation to you, O slayer of Namuci! O thousand-eyed one, consort of Śacī, salutation to you!"

sanskrit: sarpāṇāṃ sūryataptānāṃ vāriṇā tvaṃ plavo bhava tvam eva paramaṃ trāṇam asmākam amarottama
english: "Be a flood of water for the serpents scorched by the sun. You alone are our supreme protection, O best of the immortals."

sanskrit: īśo hy asi payaḥ sraṣṭuṃ tvam analpaṃ puraṃdara tvam eva meghas tvaṃ vāyus tvam agnir vaidyuto 'mbare
english: "For you are capable of creating vast waters, O Purandara. You yourself are the cloud, you are the wind, you are Agni, you are the lightning fire in the sky."

sanskrit: tvam abhraghanavikṣeptā tvām evāhuḥ punar ghanam tvaṃ vajram atulaṃ ghoraṃ ghoṣavāṃs tvaṃ balāhakaḥ
english: "You are the thrower of dense clouds, and they call you the cloud itself once again. You are the thunderbolt, incomparable and dreadful; you are the thunder-voiced rain cloud Balāhaka."

sanskrit: sraṣṭā tvam eva lokānāṃ saṃhartā cāparājitaḥ tvaṃ jyotiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvam ādityo vibhāvasuḥ
english: "You alone are the creator of the worlds and the destroyer, unconquered. You are the light of all beings; you are Āditya, the blazing fire."

sanskrit: tvaṃ mahad bhūtam āścaryaṃ tvaṃ rājā tvaṃ surottamaḥ tvaṃ viṣṇus tvaṃ sahasrākṣas tvaṃ devas tvaṃ parāyaṇam
english: "You are a great, wondrous being. You are the king, you are the best of gods. You are Viṣṇu, you are the thousand-eyed, you are the god, you are the supreme refuge."

sanskrit: tvaṃ sarvam amṛtaṃ deva tvaṃ somaḥ paramārcitaḥ tvaṃ muhūrtas tithiś ca tvaṃ lavas tvaṃ vai punaḥ kṣaṇaḥ
english: "You are all nectar, O god; you are Soma, supremely worshipped. You are the muhūrta, and the tithi; you are the lava, and the kṣaṇa."

sanskrit: śuklas tvaṃ bahulaś caiva kalā kāṣṭhā truṭis tathā saṃvatsarartavo māsā rajanyaś ca dināni ca
english: "You are the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight, the kalā, kāṣṭhā, truṭi, years, seasons, months, nights, and days."

sanskrit: tvam uttamā sagirivanā vasuṃdharā; sabhāskaraṃ vitimiram ambaraṃ tathā mahodadhiḥ satimitimiṃgilas tathā; mahormimān bahumakaro jhaṣālayaḥ
english: "You are the earth at her best with mountains and forests; you are the sky, luminous with the sun, free of darkness. You are the great ocean, filled with timi and timiṅgila fish, with great waves, many makaras, and a home for fish."

sanskrit: mahad yaśas tvam iti sadābhipūjyase; manīṣibhir muditamanā maharṣibhiḥ abhiṣṭutaḥ pibasi ca somam adhvare; vaṣaṭkṛtāny api ca havīṃṣi bhūtaye
english: "You are great glory — so you are ever worshipped by the wise and by the great ṛṣis with joyful hearts. Praised, you drink the soma at sacrifices, and the havis offered with the vaṣaṭ call for the welfare of beings."

sanskrit: tvaṃ vipraiḥ satatam ihejyase phalārthaṃ; vedāṅgeṣv atulabalaugha gīyase ca tvaddhetor yajanaparāyaṇā dvijendrā; vedāṅgāny abhigamayanti sarvavedaiḥ
english: "You are ever worshipped here by the brāhmaṇas for the sake of fruit; you are sung of in the Vedic ancillaries, O flood of incomparable strength. For your sake the twice-born lords, devoted to sacrifice, master the Vedic ancillaries together with all the Vedas."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evaṃ stutas tadā kadrvā bhagavān harivāhanaḥ nīlajīmūtasaṃghātair vyoma sarvaṃ samāvṛṇot
english: Suta said: Thus praised by Kadrū, the blessed Harivāhana covered the entire sky with masses of dark-blue clouds.

sanskrit: te meghā mumucus toyaṃ prabhūtaṃ vidyudujjvalāḥ parasparam ivātyarthaṃ garjantaḥ satataṃ divi
english: Those clouds, blazing with lightning, released abundant water and roared incessantly against one another in the sky as if competing.

sanskrit: saṃghātitam ivākāśaṃ jaladaiḥ sumahādbhutaiḥ sṛjadbhir atulaṃ toyam ajasraṃ sumahāravaiḥ
english: The sky seemed to be packed solid with those most wondrous rain-clouds, which poured forth incomparable water ceaselessly with a tremendous roar.

sanskrit: saṃpranṛttam ivākāśaṃ dhārormibhiḥ anekaśaḥ meghastanitanirghoṣam ambaraṃ samapadyata
english: The sky seemed to dance with the manifold surging waves of rain, and the firmament was filled with the resounding peal of thunder.

sanskrit: nāgānām uttamo harśas tadā varṣati vāsave āpūryata mahī cāpi salilena samantataḥ
english: The nāgas were filled with the greatest joy when Vāsava rained down; and the earth too was flooded with water on every side.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca suparṇenohyamānās te jagmus taṃ deśam āśu vai sāgarāmbuparikṣiptaṃ pakṣisaṃghanināditam
english: Suta said: Carried by Suparṇa, they quickly reached that place, which was encircled by the waters of the ocean and resounded with the cries of flocks of birds.

sanskrit: vicitraphalapuṣpābhir vanarājibhir āvṛtam bhavanair āvṛtaṃ ramyais tathā padmākarair api
english: It was covered with rows of trees bearing varied fruits and flowers, enclosed by lovely mansions, and adorned with lotus pools as well.

sanskrit: prasannasalilaiś cāpi hradaiś citrair vibhūṣitam divyagandhavahaiḥ puṇyair mārutair upavījitam
english: It was embellished with lakes of clear water of variegated beauty, and fanned by holy breezes carrying divine fragrances.

sanskrit: upajighradbhir ākāśaṃ vṛkṣair malayajair api śobhitaṃ puṣpavarṣāṇi muñcadbhir mārutoddhutaiḥ
english: It was beautified by sandal-wood trees that touched the sky with their fragrance, and which, shaken by the wind, were showering down rains of blossoms.

sanskrit: kiradbhir iva tatrasthān nāgān puṣpāmbuvṛṣṭibhiḥ manaḥsaṃharṣaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ priyam nānāpakṣirutaṃ ramyaṃ kadrūputrapraharṣaṇam
english: The showers of flowers and water seemed to be scattered over the nāgas assembled there; the place was heart-gladdening, holy, beloved of gandharvas and apsarases, resonant with the calls of many birds, lovely, and a source of delight for the sons of Kadrū.

sanskrit: tat te vanaṃ samāsādya vijahruḥ pannagā mudā abruvaṃś ca mahāvīryaṃ suparṇaṃ patagottamam
english: Having reached that forest, the serpents sported there with joy, and they also addressed the mighty Suparṇa, that best of birds.

sanskrit: vahāsmān aparaṃ dvīpaṃ suramyaṃ vipulodakam tvaṃ hi deśān bahūn ramyān patan paśyasi khecara
english: "Carry us to yet another island, most beautiful, with abundant water. For you, O sky-ranger, while flying, behold many lovely regions."

sanskrit: sa vicintyābravīt pakṣī mātaraṃ vinatāṃ tadā kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mayā mātaḥ kartavyaṃ sarpabhāṣitam
english: Reflecting on this, the bird then spoke to his mother Vinatā: "What is the reason, Mother, that I must do what the serpents say?"

sanskrit: vinatovāca dāsībhūtāsmy anāryāyā bhaginyāḥ patagottama paṇaṃ vitatham āsthāya sarpair upadhinā kṛtam
english: Vinatā said: "I have become the slave of my ignoble sister, O best of birds — a false wager was contrived by the serpents through treachery."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca tasmiṃs tu kathite mātrā kāraṇe gaganecaraḥ uvāca vacanaṃ sarpāṃs tena duḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ
english: Suta said: When the reason had been told by his mother, the sky-traveler, pained by that sorrow, spoke these words to the serpents:

sanskrit: kim āhṛtya viditvā vā kiṃ vā kṛtveha pauruṣam dāsyād vo vipramucyeyaṃ satyaṃ śaṃsata lelihāḥ
english: "By fetching what, or by knowing what, or by what act of valor here, may I be freed from slavery to you? Tell me truly, O tongue-flickering ones."

sanskrit: śrutvā tam abruvan sarpā āharāmṛtam ojasā tato dāsyād vipramokṣo bhavitā tava khecara
english: Hearing him, the serpents replied: "Bring us the amṛta by your power; then will your freedom from slavery come to pass, O sky-traveler."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ity ukto garuḍaḥ sarpais tato mātaram abravīt gacchāmy amṛtam āhartuṃ bhakṣyam icchāmi veditum
english: Suta said: Thus addressed by the serpents, Garuḍa then spoke to his mother: "I go to fetch the amṛta. I wish to know what I should eat on the way."

sanskrit: vinatovāca samudrakukṣāv ekānte niṣādālayam uttamam sahasrāṇām anekānāṃ tān bhuktvāmṛtam ānaya
english: Vinatā said: "In a secluded part of the ocean's bosom is the supreme dwelling of the Niṣādas. After eating many thousands of them, bring back the amṛta."

sanskrit: na tu te brāhmaṇaṃ hantuṃ kāryā buddhiḥ kathaṃ cana avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brāhmaṇo hy analopamaḥ
english: "But you must never under any circumstance entertain the thought of killing a brāhmaṇa. A brāhmaṇa is not to be slain by any living being, for he is inviolable and without equal."

sanskrit: agnir arko viṣaṃ śastraṃ vipro bhavati kopitaḥ bhūtānām agrabhug vipro varṇaśreṣṭhaḥ pitā guruḥ
english: "When angered, a vipra becomes fire, the sun, poison, and a weapon. The vipra is the foremost among all creatures in receiving food, the best of the varṇas, a father, a teacher."

sanskrit: garuḍa uvāca yathāham abhijānīyāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ lakṣaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ tan me kāraṇato mātaḥ pṛcchato vaktum arhasi
english: Garuḍa said: "Please tell me, Mother, since I ask — by what auspicious signs would I recognize a brāhmaṇa? You ought to explain this to me properly."

sanskrit: vinatovāca yas te kaṇṭham anuprāpto nigīrṇaṃ baḍiśaṃ yathā dahed aṅgāravat putra taṃ vidyād brāhmaṇarṣabham
english: Vinatā said: "Son, whoever, once swallowed and lodged in your throat, burns like a live coal — like a swallowed hook — him you should know to be a bull among brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca provāca cainaṃ vinatā putrahārdād idaṃ vacaḥ jānanty apy atulaṃ vīryam āśīrvādasamanvitam
english: Suta said: And Vinatā, from maternal love for her son, spoke these words to him — knowing his incomparable might — accompanied by a benediction.

sanskrit: pakṣau te mārutaḥ pātu candraḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ tu putraka śiras tu pātu te vahnir bhāskaraḥ sarvam eva tu
english: "May the wind protect your wings, and the moon your back, my son. May fire protect your head, and the sun your entire being."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca te sadā putra śāntisvastiparāyaṇā ariṣṭaṃ vraja panthānaṃ vatsa kāryārthasiddhaye
english: "And I, my son, am ever devoted to your peace and well-being. Go by an unobstructed path, dear child, to the accomplishment of your purpose."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa mātur vacanaṃ niśamya; vitatya pakṣau nabha utpapāta tato niṣādān balavān upāgamad; bubhukṣitaḥ kāla ivāntako mahān
english: Then, having heard his mother's words, he spread his wings and soared into the sky; and the powerful one approached the Niṣādas, hungry as great Death itself at the end of time.

sanskrit: sa tān niṣādān upasaṃharaṃs tadā; rajaḥ samuddhūya nabhaḥspṛśaṃ mahat samudrakukṣau ca viśoṣayan payaḥ; samīpagān bhūmidharān vicālayan
english: Driving those Niṣādas together then, he stirred up a great dust reaching to the sky, dried up the waters in the ocean's bosom, and shook the mountains standing nearby.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa cakre mahad ānanaṃ tadā; niṣādamārgaṃ pratirudhya pakṣirāṭ tato niṣādās tvaritāḥ pravavrajur; yato mukhaṃ tasya bhujaṃgabhojinaḥ
english: Then the king of birds opened his enormous mouth, blocking the path of the Niṣādas; and the Niṣādas rushed headlong toward the mouth of that devourer of serpents.

sanskrit: tadānanaṃ vivṛtam atipramāṇavat; samabhyayur gaganam ivārditāḥ khagāḥ sahasraśaḥ pavanarajobhramohitā; mahānilapracalitapādape vane
english: Into that gaping mouth of immense size they flew by the thousands, like birds flying into the sky, bewildered by the swirling dust-laden wind, like trees shaken by a great gale in the forest.

sanskrit: tataḥ khago vadanam amitratāpanaḥ; samāharat paricapalo mahābalaḥ niṣūdayan bahuvidhamatsyabhakṣiṇo; bubhukṣito gaganacareśvaras tadā
english: Then the bird, scorcher of enemies, swift and mighty, closed his mouth — slaying those who eat fish of many kinds — hungry, that lord of sky-travellers, at that moment.
